title: Niçoise Salad (Salade Niçoise)
description: A classic French salad featuring lightly seared tuna, tender vegetables, soft-boiled eggs, olives, and a traditional vinaigrette. Fresh, elegant, and beautifully balanced for a restaurant-style presentation.

ingredients.title: For the Salad
items: Yellowfin or Bluefin Tuna Loin – 200 g, fresh, sashimi grade
Fine Green Beans (Haricots Verts) – 100 g, trimmed
Soft-Boiled Quail Eggs – 6 (or 2 medium hen’s eggs)
Baby Gem Lettuce or Frisée Leaves – 1 small head
Fresh Herbs – chives, basil, tarragon (for garnish)

ingredients.title: For the Dressing (Classic French Vinaigrette)
items: Sea Salt & Cracked Black Pepper – to taste

instruction.title: Step 1 – Prepare the Tuna
steps: Lightly season tuna loin with sea salt and black pepper.
Sear on a cast-iron skillet or grill for 30–45 seconds per side, leaving the center rare.
Rest briefly, then slice into ½-inch medallions.

instruction.title: Step 2 – Prepare the Vegetables
steps: Boil potatoes in salted water until tender, drain, and toss with a touch of vinaigrette while warm.
Blanch green beans in boiling salted water for 2 minutes, then shock in ice water to retain their bright green color.
Soft-boil quail eggs (2½–3 minutes) or hen's eggs (6 minutes), then cool and peel gently.
Keep tomatoes and lettuce chilled until plating for a crisp texture.

instruction.title: Step 3 – Make the Vinaigrette
steps: Whisk Dijon mustard, red wine vinegar, lemon juice, and shallot together.
Slowly drizzle in olive oil to emulsify.

instruction.title: Step 4 – Plating
steps: On a chilled white plate, arrange lettuce as the base.
Artfully place alternating segments of tuna, potatoes, and green beans.
Add halved tomatoes, olives, capers, and eggs.
Drizzle vinaigrette in fine ribbons over and around the ingredients.
Garnish with micro herbs or chiffonade of basil and a few anchovy fillets if desired.
Optional: Finish with a few drops of aged balsamic reduction or lemon oil for aroma and sheen.

servingSuggestions.title: Serving Suggestions
items: Serve slightly chilled for the best texture and flavor.
Pair with crusty French bread or a light baguette.
Enjoy with Provence Rosé, Chablis, or a light Sauvignon Blanc.

chefTips: Always serve slightly chilled (not cold) to maintain tuna texture and vinaigrette aroma.
Use high-quality olive oil—it defines the salad's overall character.
For extra refinement, lightly brush the tuna with herb oil before searing.
